function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are enforced unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways, 55–75 mph; on rural roads, 45–65 mph; on city streets, 25–35 mph.
• “No Speed Limit” zones exist in some rural areas. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑Tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right yields.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay in their lane unless turning or merging.
• “Lane‑keeping” violations can lead to points on your license. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 2 years can result in license suspension.
• Points are assigned for speeding, reckless driving, DUI, etc. | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or on sidewalks is prohibited.
• No parking in designated handicap spaces without a valid permit. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or obstructing traffic.
• Towing a vehicle without proper authorization can lead to fines. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | | **Special Provisions** | • Texas has specific rules for “no‑stop” zones, “no‑passing” lanes, and “no‑turn” signs.
• Certain counties may have additional local ordinances. | **Where to Find Official Texts** 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Provides summaries, forms, and updates. 3. **Texas Legislature Online** – For the latest legislative changes and bill status. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Police use radar, lidar, and speed cameras for speeding enforcement. - DUI checkpoints are common, especially near major highways. - Traffic citations can be paid online, in person, or contested in court. **Legal Resources** - If you receive a ticket or are facing a traffic-related lawsuit, consult the Texas Courts website or a local attorney specializing in traffic law. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific aspect (e.g., speeding penalties, DUI statutes, or how to contest a ticket).
